label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: localrate.example/biz/harbourline-van-works
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: 3 stars - Great tub, wet floor, right call in the end

I run a mobile dog grooming van around Halifax, and Harbourline did the fitout on my Transit this summer. Tub, tanks, water heater, the whole thing.

Good stuff first, because it really is good. The stainless tub and ramp are the best thing about my van. Dogs walk right up and in on their own, and if you've ever tried to lift a big dog who doesn't want a bath, you know what that's worth.

Then came Oct 27. A little over two months after I picked the van up, the fitting on the hot water line let go in the middle of a groom. I was in Bedford with Moose, a 110 lb Bernese, in the tub. There was water all over the floor and down into the cabinet. I would love to tell you I handled it like a professional. I was screaming. Moose sat in that tub through the entire flood like a king on his throne, did not care even a little, and watched me lose it. He went home towelled off and half groomed, and I cancelled the rest of my day. His owner was lovely about it, and I'm told Moose thought it was a pool party.

Here's the thing: stuff breaks. I wasn't mad about the leak. What made me mad was the reply I got the next day. Before anyone had looked at the van, I was told these lines don't just let go, and that it's usually because the heater's been run dry or someone's been hanging stuff off the pipe. That would be user error and not covered, and there'd be a $180 diagnostic fee to look at it. I have never run it dry, and the pipe is behind a cabinet door. The earliest he could get me in was Nov 3.

I got the van back Nov 6. So I was off the road from Oct 27 to Nov 6 and lost six bookings on top of the rest of that first day. When the van is the whole business, that hurts.

Now the part that keeps this at 3 stars and not lower. Once Glenn got in there, he found the compression fitting on the outlet was a cheaper one his supplier had swapped in. He told me straight out that it was on them. He replaced all the fittings on the hot side, not just the one that failed, and took the $180 off. That's the right way to end it, and he gets full credit from me for owning it. I just wish we'd started there and not at "user error."

If you're a groomer or a tradesperson looking at them for a work vehicle, my advice is to get the warranty details in writing before you commit. The invoice says 12 months on workmanship, excluding misuse or user error. Ask what counts as user error and who decides. Ask whether you pay a diagnostic fee on a warranty claim. Ask how fast they can get you in if the van is your income, because a week's wait for a camper is annoying and a week's wait for a work van is a week of cancelled jobs.

So: the build quality on the tub and ramp is great, there was one bad fitting that turned out not to be my fault, the first response was frustrating, and it finished fairly. That makes three stars from me. Moose would give it five.
